summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with a history of primary central nervous system B-cell lymphoma was admitted for his 29th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy, along with rituximab and temozolomide. He reported ongoing stress due to a recent separation and persistent left-sided headaches, but his brain MRI remained stable with no evidence of recurrence. He experienced right upper quadrant abdominal tenderness, and an ultrasound revealed hepatic steatosis with normal liver enzymes and no gallstones. His port malfunctioned due to a fibrin sheath, requiring a successful catheter stripping procedure to restore function. Methotrexate was administered without complications, with appropriate leucovorin rescue and bicarbonate hydration. His sodium remained stable on desmopressin for diabetes insipidus, and he continued antiseizure medications without seizure activity. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete oral leucovorin and sodium bicarbonate, resume temozolomide on a 7-days-on, 7-days-off schedule, and follow up with oncology in three months.
problems: Primary central nervous system lymphoma, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites
Mechanical complication of other vascular device, implant, and graft
Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
